full_judgment: 3. Respondent No. 2 has emphatically denied petitioner's, statements that he (Respondent No. 2) is a Bihari, that his wife is also a Bihari and that he collaborated with the Pakistan Army. He was asserted that he and his wife are Bangalis. He himself hails from the District of Hoogly in West Bengal and his wife comes from the district of Faridpur in Bangladesh. He himself came to this place in 1950, got a job under the Government as a singer (now Kanthashilpi) in the then Public Relations Department (now Ministry of Information of Bangladesh) under Poet Jasimuddin and late Abbasuddin Ahmed who were in charge of Song Publicity Section and selected this respondent for this job. The respondent is now singer on Radio, TV and in public meetings of Bengali folk songs and had his training under poet Jasimuddin and late Abbasuddin Ahmed. He never concealed himself for fear of his life from 'Mukti Bahini'. Rather, after the liberation he immediately joined his office and has been rendering his humble best in the service of the nation as a singer. Sometimes he sings folk songs in public meetings, undertakes official tours with Ministers and sometimes with the Prime Minister himself. Thus the respondent No.2 controverts what has been stated against him by the petitioner.
